title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Tax-Issue Calendar Days for In-Person Sessions
content:
Two figures on the appellant's Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts record — the reserve ratio and the contribution rate — decide the tax calendar days allowed for an in-person session under Unemployment Insurance Appeals.

**Rule.** The tax calendar days are the senior tax calendar days when the appellant's tax account shows a reserve ratio below the deficit-review ratio and a contribution rate at or above the high-rate floor, the deficit calendar days when that account shows a reserve ratio below zero and a contribution rate below the high-rate floor, and zero days in every other case, including an appellant with no tax account. These days are added to the room block gap, and the set hearing date is moved later by the total before the calendar-day rule is applied.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Deficit-review ratio | -0.04 (a reserve ratio of -4.0%) |
| High-rate floor | 0.06 (a contribution rate of 6.0%) |
| Senior tax calendar | 5 calendar days |
| Deficit calendar | 2 calendar days |

## Days by reserve ratio and contribution rate

| Reserve ratio on the account | Contribution rate at or above 0.06 | Contribution rate below 0.06 |
|---|---|---|
| below -0.04 | 5 days | 2 days |
| -0.04 or above, but below zero | 0 days | 2 days |
| zero or above | 0 days | 0 days |
| no tax account | 0 days | 0 days |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical accounts)

- Reserve ratio -0.05, contribution rate 0.062 — below -0.04 and at or above 0.06: **5 days**.
- Reserve ratio exactly -0.04, contribution rate 0.065 — not below -0.04, and the rate is not below 0.06: **0 days**.
- Reserve ratio exactly -0.04, contribution rate 0.054 — below zero and below 0.06: **2 days**.
- Reserve ratio -0.01, contribution rate exactly 0.06 — the rate is at the floor, not below it, and the ratio is not below -0.04: **0 days**.
- Reserve ratio 0.02, any rate — not below zero: **0 days**.
- An appellant with no tax account: **0 days**.
